title: Block 1 · Hypertrophy
subtitle: 8 weeks + deload · Sessions A, B, C · delts, upper chest, lats and arms first
increment: 2.5 kg on a bar, the next dumbbell, or one pin

phases.1: Weeks 1–2 · Ramp-in. Every set stops 2–3 reps before failure. Log every weight: this is your baseline.
phases.3: Weeks 3–4 · Push. Machines and cables: last set to failure. Barbell: stop 1 rep short.
phases.5: Weeks 5–6 · Intensify. Same as 3–4, plus myo-reps or partials on the last set where the card says so.
phases.7: Weeks 7–8 · Peak. Same as 5–6. Beat last week on every exercise: one more rep, or a little more weight.
phases.9: Week 9 · Deload. Half the sets, same weights, stop 3–4 reps short. Then back to week 1 with your new numbers.

techniques.myo: Last set → myo-reps: hit failure, take 5 deep breaths, do 3–5 more. Repeat until you can't get 3.
techniques.partial: Last set → partials: at failure, keep going with half reps in the stretched half until it won't move.

warmup.title: Warm-up · same every day · ~5 min
steps: 3–5 min easy treadmill walk (add some incline) or bike.
First exercise: ½ your working weight × 10, then ¾ × 4.
Each new exercise after that: the card tells you if it needs a light set first. Light sets don’t count.

sessions.name: Session A
sessions.title: Session A — Bench, pull-ups, legs
sessions.focus: Strength day: your heaviest pressing and pulling while you're fresh.
sessions.short: chest, lats, quads and side delts

exercises.name: Barbell bench press
exercises.cue: Shoulder blades pinned, feet planted, touch your lower chest. This is your strength number: set the safety pins and never grind the last rep alone.
exercises.busyNote: Same lift on a fixed path, so the last set can go to failure.
exercises.noGym: Push-ups, feet on a chair, loaded backpack — 3 × 8–15
exercises.noGymNote: Too easy? Hands on two books for extra depth and a 2 s pause at the bottom.

exercises.name: Weighted pull-up
exercises.cue: Belt, or a dumbbell between your feet, heavy enough to fail near 10. Dead hang at the bottom of every rep: the stretch is where lats grow.
exercises.busyNote: Pull to your upper chest with a slight lean back. Pulldown taken too: single-arm cable pulldown, 3 × 8–12 per side.
exercises.noGymNote: No bar: inverted rows under a sturdy table, 3 × 10–15.

exercises.name: Hack squat
exercises.cue: Feet mid-platform. Sink as deep as you can with your lower back glued to the pad. No bar on your spine, so your back stays out of it.
exercises.busyNote: Both taken: Smith machine squat, feet slightly forward, 3 × 8–12.
exercises.noGym: Bulgarian split squat, loaded backpack — 3 × 10–15 per leg
exercises.noGymNote: Rear foot on a couch. A slow 3 s lowering makes it plenty hard.

exercises.name: Dumbbell lateral raise
exercises.cue: Lean forward a touch, lead with the elbows, stop at shoulder height, 2–3 s down. Side delts are what make shoulders look wide.
exercises.video: dumbbell lateral raise form Jeff Nippard
exercises.busyNote: Any version works. Keep the stop at shoulder height.
exercises.noGymNote: No band: two full water bottles, 3 s lowering, to failure.

exercises.name: Seated leg curl
exercises.cue: Seated beats lying for hamstring growth: bent hips keep them stretched. Chest slightly forward, control every rep back up.
exercises.video: seated leg curl form Jeff Nippard
exercises.busyNote: Both taken: Nordic curl negatives, 3 × 4–8, lowering in 4 s.
exercises.noGymNote: Feet under a couch, lower in 4 s, push back up with your hands. Easier: towel slider curls on a smooth floor, 3 × 10–15.

exercises.name: Overhead cable triceps extension
exercises.cue: Face away from the cable, elbows by your ears, let your hands sink deep behind your head. Grew the triceps about 40% more than pushdowns in a 12-week study.
exercises.busyNote: Stop 1–2 reps short: the weight is behind your head.
exercises.noGym: Bodyweight triceps extension on a table edge — 3 × 8–15
exercises.noGymNote: Hands on the edge, body straight, bend only at the elbows. Lower the angle to make it harder.

exercises.name: Standing calf raise
exercises.cue: Knees straight. Sink into a full stretch, hold 1–2 s, rise all the way. No bouncing.
exercises.video: standing calf raise form Jeff Nippard
exercises.busy: Calf raise on the leg press — 3 × 10–15
exercises.busyNote: Or a Smith machine calf raise on a plate. Knees straight, full stretch.
exercises.noGym: Single-leg calf raise on a step — 3 × 15–25 per leg
exercises.noGymNote: Hold a loaded backpack when 25 gets easy.

exercises.name: Kneeling cable crunch
exercises.cue: Hips stay put. Curl your ribs down toward your pelvis. Crunches thickened the abs more than leg raises in an ultrasound study.
exercises.busy: Crunch with a plate on your chest — 3 × 10–15
exercises.busyNote: On the floor or a decline bench. Same rule: stop 1–2 reps short.
exercises.noGymNote: Feet up on a couch makes it harder.

sessions.name: Session B
sessions.title: Session B — Incline, rows, legs, biceps
sessions.focus: Upper chest and back first, then a full leg session that never leaves the leg press area.
sessions.short: upper chest, back, quads and side delts

exercises.name: Smith incline press
exercises.cue: Bench at about 30°. Lower to your upper chest, elbows around 45°. Upper chest is the shelf that makes the chest look full from the front.
exercises.busyNote: With dumbbells, stop 1–2 reps short. No failure on free weights.
exercises.noGym: Decline push-ups, feet on a couch — 3 × 8–15
exercises.noGymNote: Higher feet means more upper chest. Backpack when 15 gets easy.

exercises.name: Seated cable row
exercises.cue: Let your shoulders reach forward at the stretch, then drive your elbows back. Torso stays still, which keeps your lower back out of it.
exercises.video: seated cable row form Jeff Nippard
exercises.busyNote: Chest on the pad keeps your lower back out of it.
exercises.noGymNote: Feet farther forward makes it harder.

pairs.label: Quads & side delts
pairs.note: Bring a bench and your dumbbells to the leg press. You'll use the bench again in Pair 3.

exercises.name: Leg press
exercises.cue: As deep as you can with your lower back flat on the pad. Keep the machine: calves come next on it.
exercises.busyNote: Both taken: Smith machine squat, feet forward, 3 × 8–12.
exercises.noGymNote: Loaded backpack, 3 s lowering.

exercises.name: Seated dumbbell lateral raise
exercises.cue: Sitting kills the hip swing. Elbows lead, stop at shoulder height, 2–3 s down.
exercises.busyNote: Stop at shoulder height.
exercises.noGymNote: No band: two water bottles, slow.

pairs.label: Calves & abs
pairs.note: Stay on the leg press: change the plates once, no new setup.

exercises.name: Leg press calf raise
exercises.cue: Balls of your feet on the bottom edge, knees straight, 1–2 s pause in the deep stretch.
exercises.busyNote: Or a Smith machine calf raise on a plate.
exercises.noGym: Single-leg calf raise on a step — 3 × 15–25 per leg
exercises.noGymNote: Pause 2 s at the bottom of every rep.

exercises.name: Lying reverse crunch
exercises.cue: On the bench by the leg press. Curl your pelvis up toward your ribs, lower slowly. Add ankle weights when 15 gets easy.
exercises.busyNote: Curl the pelvis up, no swinging.
exercises.noGymNote: Harder: straighter legs and a slower lowering.

pairs.label: Hamstrings & biceps
pairs.note: Grab a bench and dumbbells next to the leg curl.

exercises.name: Seated leg curl
exercises.cue: Same as Session A: squeeze hard, then fight the weight on the way back to the stretch.
exercises.video: seated leg curl form Jeff Nippard
exercises.busyNote: Both taken: Nordic curl negatives, 3 × 4–8, lowering in 4 s.
exercises.noGymNote: Feet under a couch, lower in 4 s, push back up with your hands. Easier: towel slider curls on a smooth floor, 3 × 10–15.

exercises.name: Incline dumbbell curl
exercises.cue: Bench at 45°, arms hanging behind your body. That stretched start is where the biceps grow most.
exercises.video: incline dumbbell curl form Jeff Nippard
exercises.busyNote: Face away from a low pulley, arm behind your body.
exercises.noGymNote: No bar: backpack curls, 3 s lowering, 3 × 10–15.

sessions.name: Session C
sessions.title: Session C — Delts, arms, chest & lats
sessions.focus: Frame day: extra work for shoulders, arms, chest and lats. Mostly cables and machines, quick to set up.
sessions.short: side and rear delts, chest and lats

pairs.label: Side & rear delts
pairs.note: One cable crossover for both: low pulleys for the raise, shoulder height for the fly.

exercises.name: Cable Y-raise
exercises.cue: Both arms, cables crossed from the low pulleys. Sweep out to a wide Y at shoulder height. Your widest-shoulder exercise of the week.
exercises.busyNote: Or dumbbell lateral raise. Stop at shoulder height.
exercises.noGymNote: No band: water bottles, slow lowering, to failure.

exercises.name: Reverse cable fly
exercises.cue: Cables crossed at shoulder height, arms long. Sweep back and turn your thumbs back at the end. Rear delts round the shoulder from the side.
exercises.video: reverse cable fly rear delt form
exercises.busyNote: Or chest-supported dumbbell reverse fly on a 30° bench.
exercises.noGymNote: No band: face-down Y-raises on the floor, thumbs up, 3 × 12–20.

exercises.name: Machine chest press
exercises.cue: Start from a deep stretch, no bounce at the bottom. Safe to push hard here.
exercises.busyNote: Stop 1–2 reps short with dumbbells.
exercises.noGym: Push-ups, hands on two books — 3 × to failure
exercises.noGymNote: Deeper range puts more stretch on the chest.

exercises.name: Neutral-grip lat pulldown
exercises.cue: Let the stack pull your arms all the way up, then drive your elbows down to your ribs.
exercises.busyNote: Or single-arm cable pulldown, 3 × 10–12 per side.
exercises.noGymNote: No bar: inverted rows under a table.

pairs.label: Arms
pairs.note: Same cable station: high pulley for the pushdown, low pulley for the curl.

exercises.name: Rope pushdown
exercises.cue: Elbows pinned to your sides, split the rope at the bottom. With Session A's overhead work, both triceps angles are covered.
exercises.busyNote: Or dips on the assisted machine, elbows back.
exercises.noGymNote: Or bench dips between two chairs, if your shoulders like them.

exercises.name: Bayesian cable curl
exercises.cue: Face away from a low pulley and step forward so your arm trails behind you. You curl out of the stretch.
exercises.busyNote: Bench at 45°, arms behind you.
exercises.noGymNote: No bar: backpack curls.

pairs.label: Chest & lats · stretch finish
pairs.note: Back on the crossover: low pulleys for the fly, high pulley for the pulldown.

exercises.name: Low-to-high cable fly
exercises.cue: Pulleys low, sweep your hands up to chin height. Feel the stretch across your chest at the bottom.
exercises.video: low to high cable fly form
exercises.busyNote: Or incline dumbbell fly at 30°.
exercises.noGymNote: Hands on books for depth.

exercises.name: Straight-arm cable pulldown
exercises.cue: Arms almost straight, hips back a little, sweep the bar down to your thighs. Lats only, no biceps.
exercises.busyNote: Hips low, feel the lats stretch overhead.
exercises.noGymNote: No band: slow inverted rows, 2 × 10–15.

guide.title: How to run your week
rows: A → B → C, with a rest day between when you can (Mon · Wed · Fri works). Back-to-back days are fine too.

Tap Only 2 days at the top. Session C turns blue and splits: Pairs 1–2 go after Session A, Pairs 3–4 after Session B. Do them as long as you can, and split whatever’s left into 10–15 min mini-sessions that week.
Do the session you did longest ago, in Short mode if you need it. A week like that keeps your muscle. It doesn’t undo anything.
Deload: half the sets, same weights. Then start again at week 1 with your new numbers.

guide.title: If this happens, do this
rows: Tap No gym under each exercise. Same sets and reps.
Can’t hold two stations? Do each exercise on its own: 90 s between sets, 2 min on the heavy lifts.
Under 6 h or wiped out: Short mode, every set 2–3 reps short. A short session still counts.
A twinge: stop the set and finish with the Busy version. Pain running down the leg, or still there next session: skip leg work and get it checked first.
Anywhere, and not the burn: stop that exercise and use Busy. Still hurts: skip it and write it in Notes.
Check-in: weigh in on the same scale, in the morning before eating, plus tape measurements. Send the numbers to your coach.
Sign in with the same email. Your log is saved to your account, not the phone.

footer: Your coach sees your log as you train. Week 9 done: send your coach your new measurements.
